title: A Time for Everything…
intro: Whatever season you are in, here are passages from the New Testament to meet you there. Pick what you are feeling or facing, and read what the Bible says.

groups.s: God's Word and guidance during hard times and trials

c.in: Doubt shows up in the Bible too. These passages show Jesus meeting honest questions with patience.

p.n: Thomas wants to see the wounds, Jesus meets him, and then blesses those who believe without seeing.
A father asks Jesus to help his unbelief, and Jesus heals his son.
John the Baptist, in prison, sends friends to ask whether Jesus is the one, and Jesus points to what is happening.
Many walk away, and Peter answers that there is no one else to go to.
If anyone lacks wisdom, ask God, who gives generously.

c.in: These passages are about mercy: Jesus forgiving, welcoming and restoring people who knew they had done wrong.

p.n: If we confess our sins, God is faithful and just to forgive us and cleanse us.
There is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.
Jesus tells a woman caught in adultery that he does not condemn her, and sends her on with a new start.
A woman known as a sinner weeps at Jesus's feet, and he forgives her.
A tax collector who can only ask for mercy goes home right with God.
A dying criminal asks Jesus to remember him and is promised a place in paradise.
God forgave all our trespasses and cancelled the record of debt against us.

c.b: When worry will not let go
c.in: Jesus spoke often to people who were afraid. These passages ask us to bring our worries to God and to trust him with tomorrow.

p.n: Look at the birds and the wildflowers, and do not worry about tomorrow.
Do not be anxious about anything; bring everything to God in prayer with thanks, and his peace will guard your heart.
Cast all your anxiety on God, because he cares for you.
Jesus leaves his peace with his followers and tells them not to let their hearts be troubled.
Peter walks toward Jesus on the water, begins to sink, and is caught by his hand.
Jesus is asleep in a boat in a storm, then calms the wind and the waves.
Paul reminds Timothy that God gave a spirit of power, love and self-control, not fear.

c.in: The New Testament was written to people who were suffering. These passages do not hurry past the pain, and they do speak of endurance, hope and God's nearness.

p.n: Suffering produces endurance, endurance character, and character hope, and the Spirit pours God's love into our hearts.
Paul is hard pressed but not crushed, and he fixes his eyes on what cannot be seen.
Paul pleads about his thorn, and the Lord answers that his grace is enough.
Trials test faith and build endurance, and the one who endures is blessed.
A living hope, and a faith tested by trials like gold in a fire.
Present sufferings are small beside the glory to come, and God works in all things for the good of those who love him.

c.in: The first Christians praised God in prison cells and under threat. These passages are about thanks and praise that do not wait for the trouble to pass.

p.n: Paul and Silas, beaten and in chains, pray and sing hymns at midnight, and the prison doors open.
Jesus tells his followers to rejoice and be glad when they are mistreated for his sake.
The apostles leave a beating rejoicing that they counted worthy to suffer for his name.
Do not be surprised by fiery trials; rejoice in sharing Christ's sufferings, and glorify God.
Through Jesus let us continually offer a sacrifice of praise to God.
Sing and make music in your heart, always giving thanks to God the Father.
Paul, poured out like an offering, says he is glad and rejoices with them.
A great crowd out of the great tribulation praises God, who wipes away every tear.

c.b: When you cannot see the way
c.in: If you do not know where you are headed, or feel far from where you thought you would be, these passages show a God who goes looking for people and a Savior who says he is the way.

p.n: A shepherd leaves ninety-nine sheep to find the one that wandered off.
A son who walked away is met on the road by a father who runs to him.
Jesus invites himself to Zacchaeus's house and says he came to seek and save the lost.
Jesus calls himself the good shepherd, who knows his sheep and lays down his life for them.
Thomas says they do not know the way, and Jesus answers that he is the way.
A woman searches the house for one lost coin and celebrates when she finds it.

c.b: When your heart is heavy with loss
c.in: Grief is not a lack of faith. Jesus wept at a tomb, and the writers of the New Testament speak about death honestly and with hope.

p.n: Jesus says those who mourn are blessed, for they will be comforted.
Mary falls at his feet in her grief, Jesus weeps, and then he calls Lazarus out of the tomb.
Jesus meets a widow burying her only son, feels compassion, and tells her not to weep.
God is the Father of compassion and the God of all comfort, who comforts us so that we can comfort others.
Paul writes so that believers will not grieve like people who have no hope.
Jesus tells his troubled friends that he is going to prepare a place for them.
God will wipe away every tear, and death will be no more.

c.b: When you wonder if you matter
c.in: These passages are about a love that does not depend on how we feel or how we have done. It was shown first, and shown at great cost.

p.n: God loved the world so much that he gave his Son, to save and not to condemn.
Christ died for us while we were still sinners.
Paul lists everything he can think of and says none of it can separate us from the love of God in Christ.
Paul prays that they will grasp how wide and long and high and deep Christ's love is.
John says to see what kind of love the Father has given, that we should be called his children.
God is love, and he showed it by sending his Son.
Jesus says he loves us as the Father loved him, and that no one has greater love than to lay down his life for friends.

c.b: When you are on your own
c.in: Again and again the promise is that God is with his people. These passages also show that belonging to one another is part of how God cares for us.

p.n: Jesus promises that he will not leave his followers as orphans, and that the Spirit will be with them.
Jesus ends with the promise that he is with them always, to the end of the age.
Two discouraged travelers walk to Emmaus and find that Jesus has been walking beside them.
Paul, nearly alone in prison, says the Lord stood with him and gave him strength.
God has said he will never leave or forsake us.
The church is one body with many parts, and no part can say it does not need the others.

c.in: Some of these passages offer rest and some offer a reason to keep going. Jesus himself took time away to rest.

p.n: Jesus invites the weary and burdened to come to him and find rest.
The apostles return tired, and Jesus tells them to come away and rest.
Martha is worried and busy with many things, and Jesus says only one thing is needed.
Outwardly we are wasting away, but inwardly we are renewed day by day.
Run with endurance and consider Jesus, so that you will not grow weary and lose heart.

c.in: Forgiving is hard, and these passages are honest about it. They also say why it matters and where the strength comes from.

p.n: Do not let the sun go down on your anger, and forgive one another as God forgave you.
Peter asks how often to forgive, and Jesus tells of a servant forgiven a huge debt who will not forgive a small one.
Love your enemies and do good to those who mistreat you, because God is kind even to the ungrateful.
Bless those who persecute you, and overcome evil with good.
Bear with each other and forgive as the Lord forgave you.
Be quick to listen, slow to speak and slow to anger.

c.b: When you have a decision to make
c.in: These passages are about how God guides: through his Spirit, through his word, and often a step at a time.

p.n: Do not be shaped by the world; be changed by a renewed mind, so you can discern what God wants.
Anyone who lacks wisdom can ask God, who gives to all generously.
Paul's team is held back from some roads and led by a vision to Macedonia.
Jesus says the Spirit of truth will guide his followers into all the truth.
Paul prays that their love will grow in knowledge and insight, so they can tell what is best.

c.b: When it seems no one is listening
c.in: When it seems no one is listening, the Gospels show people who cry out and are heard, and Jesus teaching that the Father pays attention.

p.n: Bartimaeus shouts from the roadside, people tell him to be quiet, and Jesus stops and calls him over.
A woman who has been ill for twelve years touches his cloak, and Jesus stops to find her and hear her story.
A widow keeps pleading for justice, and Jesus says God will see justice done for those who cry to him.
Ask, seek and knock: a father gives good gifts to his children.
When we do not know what to pray, the Spirit pleads for us with groans too deep for words.
We have a high priest who understands our weakness, so we can come to God with confidence.
John writes that we can be sure God hears us when we ask.

groups.s: God's Word to reflect on when things are good.

c.in: Thankfulness runs all through the New Testament, in songs, letters and stories.

p.n: Ten men with leprosy are healed, and only one turns back to thank Jesus.
Rejoice always, pray continually, and give thanks in all circumstances.
Let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, and be thankful.
Be rooted and built up in him, overflowing with thankfulness.
Mary's song, praising God for what he has done.
Paul ends his appeal with thanks to God for his indescribable gift.

c.in: When things are going well it is easy to drift from God. These passages gently remind us where good things come from.

p.n: Every good and perfect gift is from above, from the Father of lights.
Paul says God has not left himself without a witness: he gives rain and crops and fills hearts with joy.
Do not trust in wealth; put your hope in God, who richly provides us with everything to enjoy.
We make plans, but life is a mist, so we say, If the Lord wills.
A rich man stores up his goods and forgets that his life is not his own.
Paul says people knew God, yet did not honor him or give thanks.
Herod accepts praise as a god and does not give the glory to God.
The church at Laodicea says, I am rich, and does not see how much it needs Jesus; he stands at the door and knocks.

c.in: Jesus says that greatness is service. These passages are about using what you have been given for other people.

p.n: The Son of Man came not to be served but to serve and to give his life for many.
Jesus washes his disciples' feet and tells them to do as he has done.
A Samaritan stops to help a wounded stranger, and Jesus tells his listener to go and do the same.
Whatever you did for the least of these, you did for Jesus.
Paul recalls Jesus saying it is more blessed to give than to receive.
Whoever sows generously will reap generously, and God loves a cheerful giver.
Each of you should use whatever gift you have received to serve others.
Let us love not only in word but in action and truth.
Do not forget to do good and to share, for God is pleased with such sacrifices.
Let your light shine so that others see your good works and praise your Father.

c.in: These passages are about noticing people who are hurting and doing something: carrying burdens, sharing comfort, and showing up.

p.n: Carry each other's burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.
Rejoice with those who rejoice and mourn with those who mourn.
Encourage the disheartened, help the weak, be patient with everyone.
Four friends carry a paralyzed man to Jesus and lower him through a roof.
Peter tells a lame beggar, What I have I give you, and lifts him to his feet.
Pure religion is to look after orphans and widows in their distress.
Keep loving one another, welcome strangers, and remember those in prison as if you were there with them.
God comforts us so that we can comfort others with the comfort we have received.
If someone has the world's goods and sees a brother in need, how can God's love be in him?
When you give a banquet, invite the poor, the crippled and the blind.

c.b: The way down is the way up
c.in: Jesus taught and showed that the first will be last. These passages are about putting others first.

p.n: Think of others as better than yourselves, as Jesus did, who gave up his place and became a servant.
Jesus says that the greatest in the kingdom is the one who is humble like a child.
At a dinner, Jesus tells guests not to take the best seats, because those who humble themselves will be honored.
God opposes the proud and gives grace to the humble.
Clothe yourselves with humility toward one another, and God will lift you up in due time.

c.in: Joy in the New Testament is often a shared thing: shepherds, friends at a wedding, heaven itself.

p.n: Shepherds hear good news of great joy and go to see the child.
At a wedding, Jesus turns water into wine and gives the party its best wine.
Jesus says he has told them these things so that his joy may be in them and their joy may be full.
The seventy return full of joy, and Jesus tells them to rejoice that their names are written in heaven.
Rejoice in the Lord always.
May the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace as you trust in him.
Though you have not seen him, you love him and rejoice with joy that words cannot hold.

c.in: Hope in the New Testament is not wishing. It is confidence in what God has promised.

p.n: All creation waits in hope, and we hope for what we do not yet see.
We have been born again to a living hope and an inheritance that cannot fade.
Hope is an anchor for the soul, firm and secure.
God's grace has appeared, and we wait for the blessed hope.
Paul calls believers to put on the hope of salvation as a helmet and to encourage one another.
The river of the water of life and the tree of life, and God's servants will see his face.

c.b: When the work is worth it
c.in: For anyone who is serving, building, teaching or raising a family and wondering whether it counts: these passages say it does.

p.n: Stand firm, because your labor in the Lord is not in vain.
Do not grow weary of doing good, because in due time we will reap, and do good to everyone.
God, who began a good work in you, will carry it on to completion.
Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as for the Lord.
God will not forget your work and the love you have shown for his name.
Paul says he has not arrived, but presses on toward the goal.
Near the end, Paul looks back: he has fought the good fight, finished the race, and kept the faith.
Hold on to hope, and spur one another on to love and good deeds.

c.in: Contentment is something Paul says he had to learn. These passages are about peace with God and freedom from the chase for more.

p.n: We have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.
Paul has learned to be content in every situation, and says he can do all things through Christ who strengthens him.
Godliness with contentment is great gain.
Jesus tells of a rich man who stored up goods for himself and was not rich toward God.
Jesus says that in him we may have peace, even though in the world we have trouble.

c.in: Jesus said the whole law hangs on loving God and neighbor. These passages show what that looks like.

p.n: Paul's famous description of love, and why love outlasts everything else.
Asked for the greatest commandment, Jesus answers with love of God and love of neighbor.
A new command: love one another as Jesus has loved you.
Love must be sincere: hold on to what is good, honor one another, and be generous and hospitable.
We love because he first loved us, and we cannot love God and hate a brother or sister.

c.in: The Gospels show Jesus praying and teaching others to pray. These passages are a good place to start.

p.n: Jesus teaches to pray simply and in private, and gives the Lord's Prayer.
A disciple asks to be taught to pray, and Jesus gives a prayer and a story about asking boldly.
Jesus gets up early and goes to a quiet place to pray.
Bring every request to God with thanks, and his peace will guard your heart and mind.
Jesus prays for everyone who will believe through his followers' message.
Pray when you are in trouble, when you are happy and when you are sick; the prayer of a righteous person is powerful.

c.in: Faith in the New Testament is trust in God and his promises, and it shows itself in action.

p.n: Faith is being sure of what we hope for, and without it no one can please God.
Abraham was fully convinced that God could do what he had promised.
A Roman officer trusts that Jesus only needs to say the word, and Jesus is amazed at his faith.
Jesus says to have faith in God and to pray with confidence.
The apostles ask for more faith, and Jesus speaks of a mustard seed.
Faith without actions is dead.

c.in: The Bible treats wisdom as a way of living, not only as knowledge.

p.n: Two builders: the wise one hears Jesus's words and acts on them, building on rock.
Wisdom from above is pure, peaceable, gentle and full of good fruit.
Be careful how you live, make the most of every opportunity, and understand what the Lord wants.
Be wise toward outsiders, and let your speech be gracious and seasoned with salt.
The message of the cross looks foolish to many, yet it is the power and wisdom of God.

c.in: The first Christians faced real danger. These passages are about courage that comes from trusting God.

p.n: Do not be afraid of those who can only harm the body; you are worth more than many sparrows.
After a threat, the church prays for boldness, and the place where they meet is shaken.
Be strong in the Lord and put on the full armor of God.
Be alert, stand firm in the faith, be courageous and do everything in love.

c.in: These passages describe what is true of believers because of what Christ has done: forgiven, adopted, new and held.

p.n: Saved by grace through faith, and made God's handiwork for good works.
Those led by the Spirit are children of God and heirs with Christ.
To all who received him, he gave the right to become children of God.
Paul says he has been crucified with Christ, and that Christ lives in him.
All who are in Christ Jesus are children of God and one in him.
Anyone in Christ is a new creation, reconciled to God and given the message of reconciliation.
You are a chosen people and a royal priesthood, called out of darkness into his light.
Your life is hidden with Christ in God, so set your mind on things above.

c.in: Jesus was tempted too. These passages are about resisting, about where strength comes from, and about not walking the road alone.

p.n: Jesus is tempted in the wilderness and answers each time with Scripture.
No temptation is beyond what people can bear, and God provides a way out.
Blessed is the one who stands the test, and desire, when it grows, leads to sin and death.
Jesus tells his friends to watch and pray so they will not fall into temptation.
Walk by the Spirit, and the fruit of the Spirit grows in place of the works of the flesh.
Do not let sin reign in your body; offer yourselves to God, for sin will not be your master.

c.b: When you want to begin again
c.in: New beginnings are a steady theme in the New Testament: new birth, a new way of living, and a Father who welcomes people home.

p.n: Jesus tells Nicodemus that a person must be born again.
A son returns home, and his father welcomes him back with a feast.
We were buried with Christ so that we too might live a new life.
Put off the old self and put on the new, made to be like God in true righteousness and holiness.
Jesus calls Simon Peter, who feels unworthy, and tells him not to be afraid.
